clue.text: A theatre emptied by prudish church leader

parts.note: prudish means prim, primly proper
taken as written

indicators.note: a word emptied loses all its inside letters, keeping only its two ends

explanation.surface: A prudish bishop takes offence at a play and walks out, leaving the theatre empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' keeps only the first and last letters of 'theatre', TE; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop or the most senior bishop of a province, so a leader of a church.

clue.text: Miserable friend — Conservative losing love

parts.note: pal means friend

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A friend is miserable as the Conservative loses a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes O from TORY, leaving TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry and miserable both describe a meagre, pitifully small amount.

clue.text: Simple manoeuvres for forces

indicators.note: manoeuvres move things about, so the word's letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Simple military movements carried out by armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges SIMPLE; 'forces' looks like soldiers but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act, so forces in the verb sense.

clue.text: Better make a speech after running a mile

indicators.note: after means the speech piece follows the scrambled letters
running suggests movement and disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: to orate is to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: Giving a speech after running a mile might be better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges A MILE into AMELI; 'Better' is a verb, to improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve something, to make it better.

clue.text: Looking at, for example, embracing Chinese principle

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: yin is the feminine principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Looking at an example that embraces a Chinese idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Eying is a spelling of eyeing, watching or regarding closely.

clue.text: Senior churchman accepts notice quietly, with a straight face

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the churchman's word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a dean is the senior clergyman of a cathedral
AD is short for advertisement, a notice
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A senior cleric quietly receives news, keeping his expression blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan describes humour or a manner delivered with no expression, a straight face.

clue.text: Brief affair of union supporting Germany

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
an alliance is a union of parties

explanation.surface: A short liaison involving a union that backs Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual or brief romantic or sexual relationship.

clue.text: Second to interrupt when showing book

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A second interruption occurs while a book is being shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Sorry, seeing quote put up after course

indicators.note: after places the turned word following the course

parts.note: a path is a course or route

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means written upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Apologising, having seen a quotation posted after a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns CITE into ETIC; 'Sorry' means pitiful, not apologetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry can mean wretched or pitiful, as in a sorry sight.

clue.text: Absence of touch, for example, is baloney!

parts.note: non- is a prefix meaning absence or lack
touch is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Claiming a lack of the sense of touch, for example, is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Baloney is slang for foolish talk or rubbish.

clue.text: The French framing a note in error

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so the French article surrounds what follows

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
taken as written
PS, postscript, is a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: French people framing a musical note mistakenly, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or small mistake, an error of attention.

clue.text: Criminally obtained title long challenged

indicators.note: something challenged is disputed and unsettled, so these letters are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A title long held is challenged as having been criminally acquired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'challenged' rearranges the nine letters of TITLE LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten gains are those acquired dishonestly or illegally.

clue.text: Drunk chased by partner, initially with popular item of kitchenalia

indicators.note: to be chased is to have something come after you, so the next pieces follow

parts.note: 'rolling drunk' gives rolling as slang for very drunk

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word partner

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A drunk followed by a partner wielding a kitchen utensil: a comic-strip scene of a spouse awaiting a late return.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the cartoon wife waiting with a rolling pin for her drunken husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling pin is a cylinder used in the kitchen for flattening pastry, a classic utensil.

clue.text: Give up, as chef does on and off

indicators.note: on and off means intermittently, so only every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Surrendering, as a cook does now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of CHEF DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield territory or a right.

clue.text: Places outside European-sounding inspections

indicators.note: outside means the places word goes round the other piece

parts.note: spots are places or locations

indicators.note: sounding means we want a word pronounced the same as the nationality

parts.note: a Czech is a European, from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: Inspections at sites outside that sound European.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot checks are random, unannounced inspections.

clue.text: Greece, in debt to Spain, possibly having teething problems

parts.note: GR is the international abbreviation for Greece
owing means still in debt to someone

indicators.note: possibly signals that the country's letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Greece, owing money to Spain, has early troubles: a picture of eurozone debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing pains are early difficulties of a new venture, like the troubles of teething.

clue.text: Getting rid of branch employing Greek character abroad

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the letter is taken into the branch word

parts.note: a wing is a branch of an organisation or building
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
out can mean abroad, away from home

explanation.surface: A branch office employs a Greek person working overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiping out means eliminating or destroying completely.

clue.text: Launch scheme for such an office

parts.note: to open something is to launch it
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: Launching a scheme for an office layout of that kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the adjective describing the office; 'for' links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-plan describes an office with no internal walls, one large shared room.

clue.text: Secret society avoided getting caught inside

indicators.note: inside places the cricket letter within the avoided word

parts.note: eluded means avoided or escaped
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A secret society evaded capture, having someone caught inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret society' looks like one phrase, but Secret is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded place is private and hidden away, so secret.

clue.text: Quite attractive? Maybe too twee

parts.note: pretty can mean quite, as in 'pretty good'
pretty means attractive or good-looking

explanation.surface: Is it quite attractive, or perhaps excessively sweet?
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty-pretty describes something prettified to excess, overly dainty or sentimental.

clue.text: What might be left by Eastern nation?

parts.note: a state is a nation

explanation.surface: Asks what an Eastern nation might leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is all the property bequeathed after their death.

clue.text: The girl's supporting American guides

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece goes beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: hers means belonging to the girl

explanation.surface: A girl's support for American tour guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers show people to their seats, so they guide them.

clue.text: Nothing to the west of European river

indicators.note: in an across entry west is the left, so this piece comes first

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Nothing lies westward of a European river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river flowing north through Egypt.

clue.text: Troubled, as it is then quite the contrary?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the following letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks, worried, whether things are now the exact opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is the direct opposite of something, its contrary.

clue.text: Incompetent writer held up by it

indicators.note: held means gripped, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a writer

explanation.surface: An incompetent author is delayed by technology.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the writer; 'held ... by' wraps the pronoun 'it' around that, with 'it' supplying its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, so incompetent.

clue.text: Biblical character taken in by apples — a usurper?

indicators.note: taken in by means contained within, so the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A Bible figure seduced by apples, who turns out to be a usurper.
explanation.walkthrough: Esau was Jacob's brother, cheated of his birthright: Jacob, not Esau, was the usurper.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau is the elder son of Isaac in Genesis who sold his birthright.

clue.text: Something that attracts many on the air — quality

indicators.note: on the air means broadcast, spoken out, so a word is replaced by one that is pronounced alike

parts.note: loads means a great many
tone is a quality of sound or character

explanation.surface: Something that draws many listeners to a broadcast with its quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is naturally magnetic rock, and figuratively anything that draws people.

clue.text: Stop patient eating last of cheese

indicators.note: eating takes food inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a case is a patient being treated by a doctor

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word cheese

explanation.surface: Telling a patient to stop eating cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to stop or come to an end.

clue.text: Admittedly bound to change

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An admission that something is certain to alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges BOUND TO; 'bound to' looks like part of the phrase but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: No doubt can concede a point, meaning admittedly or granted.

clue.text: Tea judges perhaps set rats scurrying

indicators.note: scurrying rats run about in all directions, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tea judges perhaps send rats running about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scurrying' rearranges SET RATS; 'perhaps' marks tea judges as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional tea tasters judge blends, one example of people who sample for quality.
